father_note: Zinn is your blood-sister and she will stand for you before anyone else in this village does — go to her first when you don't know who to trust. Sela fed me when she didn't have to, and that is a debt I pass to you. Watch Bram: he has never moved against us, but he has called off two fights when the numbers turned, which tells you he counts before he commits — respect that, but don't lean on it. Hold enough food to eat, give just enough to be remembered, and don't let anyone see you hungry if you can help it.

memory_raw.text: Talia (female, age 21; str 64, int 5070, mem 18061; O58 C54 E47 A56 N48) is born to Sela and Mako.

Zinn, Fina is sitting on twenty-four food and no one in this village has ever held that much at once — I don't know if she's brilliant or building a wall between herself and the rest of us, but either way I want to understand her before someone like Bram decides to.
Fina, I've been watching you — not in a bad way, the way you watch someone who seems to know something you don't — and I wanted to ask you straight: how did you get to twenty-four?
Mako gathers Zinn, Talia to talk.

Talia, you came into this world today and I'm your father — whatever you hear from others about this village, you come to me or Zinn first. Zinn, she's blood to both of us now; keep her close to Nessa's circle and away from Bram until she finds her feet.

Mako, I hear you — and I already went to Zinn before you called us here, so maybe your blood runs truer in me than I knew. I want to understand Fina before anyone else does; she's holding twenty-five food and that's either the safest person in this village to stand near or the most dangerous, and I can't tell which yet.

Fina's neither safe nor dangerous yet — she's deciding, and a woman with that much food and no man to answer to is listening for who speaks to her like a person instead of a prize. Talia, you're new and you don't carry my weight with her; that's worth something. Go to her through Nessa, say nothing about food, and just let her see your face a few times before the year closes.

Nessa's already given me something to work with — she's been feeding Fina steady, so there's a thread there I can pull without it looking like I'm pulling anything. I'll go sit near them, let Fina notice me first, and keep my mouth shut about food even if it's the only thing anyone's thinking about. Zinn, if Fina asks you about me before I get close enough to speak for myself, tell her something plain — not flattering, just true.

Zinn, what's plain and true about Talia is that she came into this room asking the right questions before I even knew to ask them — tell Fina that, if she asks, because a woman who counts food the way Fina does will respect someone who counts people the same way. Talia, you've got the right instinct with Nessa, just don't move so careful that you look like you're moving careful.

Mako, when you say don't move so careful that I look careful — that's harder than it sounds for someone who came into this world today with everyone already watching. Zinn, you know me better than anyone here does; am I the kind of person who can walk into a circle without making it obvious I want to be in it?
Mako, you have nothing left and I have five — take two from me now, before the year closes and you're eating air.
Year 14: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Kael takes 4 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Talia takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Zinn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Mako gathers Zinn, Talia to talk.

Pile's gone again and I've got two food — I'm not thin yet but I'm not sitting easy either. Talia, you took three from the pile which is right; Zinn, you've got three and Nessa gave you one already, so that's four — that's where I want you both before I start worrying about anything else. Tell me what you each saw when Kael took four.

Kael took four before half the village had moved — he wasn't grabbing out of panic, he was counting ahead, and a man who counts ahead in a thin year is either planning to weather it alone or planning to have something to offer someone. He's got four now and he held it quiet after; no giving, no talking. I don't know his angle yet but I'd want to know it before next year's pile drops.

Kael's fifty-eight and he took four — a man that age doesn't save food for a child offer, so he's either building a wall around himself for a thin year or he's got an eye on someone's food and wants weight behind him when he moves. Zinn, has he spoken to you at all this year, anything that looked like feeling out where you stand? I want to know if he's circling before he knows we're watching.

Zinn, while Mako waits on your answer — I want to say that if Kael's counting bodies before he moves, he's counting mine as new and unattached, which makes me either easy to ignore or easy to approach. If he does circle, I'd rather he find me already standing somewhere he didn't expect.

Zinn, say your piece — I'm not moving anything until I hear it, but while we wait I want Talia to know this: "standing somewhere he didn't expect" means standing with us visibly, so that Kael counts you as attached before he decides to test it. One food moving between you and Zinn in the open today does more than anything we say in here.

Mako's right — I'll give Zinn one food in the open before this day closes, and I'd rather do it where Kael can see it than where he can't. But Zinn, I still want your read on him; you've been in this village longer than I have and you know what a man looks like when he's building toward something versus just hoarding against a hard year.

Zinn hasn't spoken yet and I'm not going to keep talking into her silence — Zinn, one word is enough, even just whether he's looked at you differently since the pile dropped. Talia, give her the food in the open like you said; I'll be where I can be seen when you do it.
Zinn, I'm going to give you that food right now whether you answer or not — but I'd sleep easier tonight knowing you'd noticed something about Kael, even nothing, because nothing is also an answer.

Zinn's been quiet too long and I'm done waiting on it — Talia, give her the food now and let's close this room. What I know is this: Kael's got four food, no allies I can name, and he's fifty-eight years old in a village where men his age start dying on their own, so whatever he's counting toward, we're not it.

Mako, I hear you — we're done talking about Kael for now, and you're right that he's probably just a man getting old and scared. But I want you to eat before we scatter; you said two food and I'm watching you hold it like it's someone else's.

mother_note:
Talia, you come from Mako's strength and my stubbornness, and both of those will keep you alive if you let them work together.

Your blood is Nessa, Zinn, and me — Zinn will tell you the truth even when it costs her, and Nessa will love you with everything she has while keeping half of herself behind a door she won't open; love them both, but lean on Zinn when you need someone who will say the hard thing out loud.

Your father Mako has fed his children before himself since before you were born, and Fina — Nessa's daughter, your niece by blood — is one to watch for, because she moves carefully and feeds people she doesn't have to.

Bram has tried to take from this family twice and been turned back both times by numbers; he is not your enemy unless you let yourself stand alone, so never stand alone.
name: Talia
